questions.q: 2-Bromo-1,1-diphenylethene is heated with sodium alkoxide. The organic product is:
questions.explain: The base removes the vinylic H and bromide leaves from the same carbon; a phenyl group then shifts across to give the C≡C, so the two phenyls end up on different carbons of the alkyne.

questions.q: Which description best fits the key elimination step of the Fritsch–Buttenberg–Wiechell rearrangement?
options: β-Elimination of H and X from adjacent carbons (E2)
Syn elimination through a cyclic transition state
E1 elimination through a vinyl cation
α-Elimination of H and X from the same carbon, giving a vinylidene carbene or carbenoid
questions.explain: The carbon bearing X carries the only H and the other alkene carbon has no H, so β-elimination is impossible. H and X leave from the same carbon and the electron-deficient centre is repaired by a 1,2-shift.

questions.q: In the FBW rearrangement of a 1,1-diaryl-2-bromoethene, which aryl group migrates?
options: The aryl group cis to the bromine
Always the more electron-rich aryl group
The aryl group trans to the bromine
Both migrate equally, regardless of geometry
questions.explain: The group trans to the leaving halogen is the one that migrates; the cis group does not migrate well. Geometry, not electronics, is the deciding factor here.

questions.q: A substrate (Ar)(Ar′)C=CHBr, with two different aryl groups, is treated with n-BuLi at low temperature. The alkyne obtained is:
options: Ar–C≡C–Ar if Ar′ is trans to Br
A 1 : 1 mixture of Ar–C≡C–Ar and Ar′–C≡C–Ar′
questions.explain: Whichever aryl shifts, both aryl groups end up on the triple bond, so the product is the same unsymmetrical alkyne Ar–C≡C–Ar′. No aryl group is lost and no symmetrical alkyne can form from a single molecule.
